chapter: N'goma drums and the scrapbook clippings
title: Paul Lavalle's letter about jury duty and the City Service Band
summary: A 1952 letter from Lavalle asks a court to postpone Morehouse's jury service because he was a featured soloist on the weekly City Service broadcasts.

blocks.x: spaghetti and hot sausages. The clipping continues on the other side but he's got it folded over. So I can't read it and I don't want to undo his scrapbook. Along with a photograph of the City Service Band of America, conducted by Paul Lavalle, there is a copy of a letter written by Paul Lavalle on his letterhead with the address, 30 Rockefeller Plaza, New York 20, N.Y., dated October 10, 1952, addressed to Presiding Judge, Supreme Court, State of New York, Queens County, General Courthouse, Sutphen Boulevard and 88th-89th Avenue, Jamaica, Queens, N.Y. "Sir: Mr. Chauncey Morehouse has advised me he has received a jury summons which commences October 14, 1952. Mr. Morehouse is an integral member of my organization, the Band of America, on our weekly coast to coast broadcasts which are sponsored by the City Service Gas and Oil Company. Our programs are arranged and planned weeks in advance. And it is therefore impossible to make last minute changes, particularly in the case of Mr. Morehouse, for he is a featured soloist on every broadcast. It is of course impossible to replace him at this time. And it becomes quite a problem because it involves a cast of 52 people. In view of this, I do hope that you will be able to postpone Mr. Morehouse's jury duty. Respectfully yours, Paul Lavalle, Conductor of the City Service Band of America." I asked Chauncey last night if the letter succeeded in getting him a postponement of jury duty. He said it did.
